articles.title: House Democrats Open Inquiry After Incoming Lawmaker Accused of Sexual Harassment
articles.summary: The House Democratic campaign arm is looking into an allegation against Representative-elect Brian Poindexter of Ohio. His campaign says he “gave what he thought was an innocuous compliment to a volunteer.”

articles.title: La Maison Blanche annonce une rencontre trilatérale entre Donald Trump, Vladimir Poutine et Xi Jinping, le 19 novembre en Chine
articles.summary: Washington a précisé que les discussions des trois présidents, en marge du sommet de l’APEC à Shenzhen, porteraient sur le désarmement nucléaire. Selon un responsable américain, s’exprimant sous couvert d’anonymat, l’Iran sera aussi au menu de la rencontre, mais pas l’Ukraine.

articles.title: Nvidia Scandal Prompts Questions of What It Means to Be a Spy
articles.summary: U.S. intelligence agencies believe a woman who had an affair with Jensen Huang was a Chinese asset. But there is much more that they are still assessing about her role.

articles.title: Un navire-citerne percute un bateau de croisière à La Nouvelle-Orléans, aucun blessé grave
articles.summary: Douze personnes ont été sorties de l’eau, et 32 personnes ont été transportées à l’hôpital. La collision a eu lieu alors que le bateau de la compagnie American Cruise Lines était amarré à quai, sur le Mississippi, avec ses passagers à bord.

articles.title: Après la Finlande et la Norvège, la Suède veut empêcher les athlètes russes de concourir sur son sol
articles.summary: Stockholm souhaite présenter prochainement une « solution consistant à refuser l’entrée de son territoire aux athlètes russes », a annoncé le ministre des affaires sociales et de la santé publique, Jakob Forssmed. La mesure devrait être effective avant les championnats du monde de ski nordique, en février.

articles.title: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test
articles.summary: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean.

articles.title: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision
articles.summary: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.

articles.title: The Numbers Behind Scott Colom’s Stunning Upset in the Mississippi Senate Race
articles.summary: To win a Senate seat in a highly polarized, deeply Republican state, Scott Colom needed a perfect storm. He got it.

articles.title: Trump Officials Press Congress to Renew Spying Law in Lame-Duck Session
articles.summary: The request to extend a high-profile warrantless surveillance law would add a thorny issue during waning Republican control.

articles.title: 5 Takeaways from Joe Biden’s Memoir: The Debate, Dropping Out and Advice From Romney
articles.summary: The 46th president defends his decision to run for re-election, which many in his party now regard as a mistake, and revisits the disastrous debate that forced him to end his campaign.

articles.title: Democrats Vie for Support in Race for Top Senate Job
articles.summary: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said he wouldn’t run for president to focus on his leadership challenge to Senator Chuck Schumer, who remained confident he would prevail.

articles.title: L’armée américaine intervient pour une « suspicion d’activité de drone non autorisée » au-dessus d’une base militaire britannique
articles.summary: « Aucun membre du personnel, aucun avion ni aucune infrastructure n’a été touché », a fait savoir un porte-parole de l’armée de l’air américaine, une fois l’incident résolu. La base concernée se situe à Lakenheath, dans l’est de l’Angleterre.

articles.title: US Air Force says it responded to 'suspected drones' over RAF Lakenheath
articles.summary: The American military says there were no injuries or damage after "suspected unauthorised drone activity" this evening.

articles.title: Le Burkina Faso annonce lancer des mandats d’arrêt contre des journalistes et des activistes en exil pour des faits de « terrorisme »
articles.summary: Les autorités de la junte d’Afrique de l’Ouest ciblent une vingtaine de personnes, et demandent leur extradition. Un chroniqueur burkinabé de RFI et des anciens ministres de l’ex-président Blaise Compaoré sont notamment visés.

articles.title: Microsoft outage 'stark reminder' of how much we rely on tech
articles.summary: Microsoft has apologised for the issue, which it said was due to a technical failure.

articles.title: African Miss Universe Contestants Struggle to Get U.S. Visas
articles.summary: A crackdown on entry by some citizens of African countries by the U.S. immigration officials means that some contestants might not get visas in time to attend the pageant in Puerto Rico this month.

articles.title: Supreme Court Set to Hear Trump’s Ban on Asylum Claims at Border
articles.summary: Lower courts have ruled against the policy, which has effectively shut down avenues for people seeking asylum protections and to remain in the United States.

articles.title: Watch: How the Microsoft outage affected North America
articles.summary: The BBC's Nadine Yousif's reports that Microsoft services like Outlook are slowly coming back online, but the company noted users "may still experience intermittent access issues".

articles.title: Two horses briefly board public bus in Detroit
articles.summary: The city said it will provide additional training for bus drivers after CCTV footage revealed the moment the horses and their riders walk onto the bus.
